comment: What the cosmetic_filtering check expects of /cosmetic/index.html. 'hidden' are ad containers that the pinned EasyList hides on any site ('rule' is the line in overlay/third_party/filter_lists/easylist.txt; tests/test_bench_cosmetic.py checks that it is there). 'case' says how the page attacks the hide: 'attacked' elements are in the markup, and a few seconds after load the page empties adoptedStyleSheets, removes its own style elements and its own link to page.css, and forces 'display:block !important' on them; 'late' elements do not exist until the page's script inserts them, after the browser's load-time passes; a 'late-class' element is in the markup with an ordinary class, and the page's script adds the ad class to it later. 'visible' are first-party elements, with names that merely look like ad names, that must stay. 'hijack_flag' is a window property that the page's own scripts set if they can intercept the injection: it must stay unset. 'attack_flag' and 'late_flag' are set by the page once the attack and the late insert ran; a run where they are unset proves nothing and fails. 'generic_sheet_probe' is a selector that only the generic hide sheet names; the check counts the rules with origin 'user-agent' (where Blink reports user-origin sheets) for it that match the element and expects one.

hidden.via: generic class rule, element inserted late
generic id rule, inside a wrapper inserted late
generic class rule, class added later to an element that was already there
